items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: the experience with Ray Noble... he and Claude Thornhill didn't get on too well... we had these sort of plastic-paper combination like music cases... Ray and his orchestra

ctx.x: Once he stopped he was able to go out and become a big success. But there are so many funny stories of course to tell about the experience with Ray Noble, as I say he was a great musician and he wrote some beautiful songs, but he and Claude Thornhill didn't get on too well and I will never forget the night Claude left. Now In the Rainbow Room you had a big stage like in the back, on either side of the platform stage were two flights of stairs and the acts would or were run up under a spotlight, They would come…

Some of the best acts in the world and it was so funny to hear Ray Noble introducing these acts, 'Now, ladies and gentlemen, from the continental (unintelligible) we have so and so, and the people didn't have the faintest idea what he was saying. It was all a lot of fun.
